To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the major risk factors are as prevalent in the elderly as the young, that the risk profiles of older persons predict cardiovascular events as efficiently as the younger, that recurrent cardiovascular events also are predicted by these same risk factors, and that the recent declines in coronary mortality include the elderly.

the major risk factors apply equally to the elderly as to the young; that these risk factors are highly and frequently present in the elderly; and that the risk of cardiovascular disease is doubled in the elderly at any given level of risk factors, compared with the young.

the risk factors for cardiovascular disease in the young and old are the same; the prevalence of risk factors is high in the elderly and is increasing as the population ages; the incidence of cardiovascular disease increases with age and with the number of risk factors; the same risk factors predict recurrent events in the elderly as do initial events; and the decline in coronary and stroke incidence in the elderly is consistent with the decline in risk factors in the middle aged.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the epidemiology of cardiovascular disease, the risk factors for its occurrence, and its prevention.
the epidemiology of cardiovascular disease, including the role of risk factors, and the prevention of coronary heart disease in the elderly.
the epidemiology of cardiovascular disease and its risk factors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cardiovascular risk factors are as important in the elderly as they are in the young, and the same interventions are indicated.
the risk factors that apply in the young also apply in the elderly, and that the risk profiles of the elderly are as predictive as those of the young.
the major risk factors apply to the elderly as well.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the epidemiologic data support the view that the major risk factors for coronary and stroke are as relevant to the elderly as to the middle aged.
the major risk factors apply to the elderly as well, and there is a need for further research on modifying these risk factors in the old.
cardiovascular disease in the aged is a preventable disease, and the major risk factors apply to the aged as well as the middle aged.

risk factors for cardiovascular disease apply to the elderly as well.
